title: Add reference track and colored mismatches
description: Use --reference FASTA to draw a visible reference-base track and color read bases that differ from the reference by nucleotide identity.
close_reason: Added FASTA-backed reference track and reference-aware mismatch coloring with tests and docs.

title: Stabilize feature track rendering
description: Exon models can flicker while navigating because grouped feature model ordering is not fully deterministic across render passes. Make feature row ordering stable and avoid suppressing unrelated gene records.
close_reason: Feature track row ordering is deterministic and grouped exon models no longer hide unrelated gene rows.

title: Render transcript exon models
description: Render grouped transcript models with intron backbones and exon/CDS/UTR blocks on the same row, so exon-intron structure is easier to read than independent feature records.
close_reason: Grouped transcript models now render intron backbones and exon/CDS/UTR blocks on the same row, with tests for grouping and duplicate suppression

title: Clarify exon and intron rendering
description: Make the annotation feature track distinguish exon blocks from intron/transcript connector lines instead of rendering all features with the same arrow body.
close_reason: Feature track now renders transcript/gene backbones as intron lines with strand ticks and exons/CDS/UTR as distinct blocks

title: Support plain and gzipped GTF/GFF loading
description: Load annotation files from plain text or gzip/BGZF streams and parse both GFF3 key=value and GTF key "value" attributes so --gff works with common .gtf.gz files.
close_reason: Plain and gzip/BGZF GFF3/GTF loading implemented with GTF attributes and tests

title: Fix TUI panic on unchecked render/event paths
description: The terminal browser can panic with index out of bounds during interactive use. Harden unchecked render indices and fix event handling so one poll consumes one event.
close_reason: Fixed unchecked render/event paths and verified with cargo fmt/test

title: GFF3: parser, feature store, gene jump
description: Add noodles-gff, parse GFF3 into feature index, jump-to-gene by name/ID, render features track in TUI
close_reason: Closed

title: Core modules: cli, app, error, region
description: Scaffold cli.rs, app.rs, error.rs, region.rs with types and parsers
close_reason: Closed

title: Cargo.toml: add all dependencies
description: Add noodles, ratatui, crossterm, clap, anyhow, thiserror to Cargo.toml
close_reason: Closed

title: Use shared-gap insertion expansion
description: Insertion expansion should match IGV-style behavior: expanding an insertion creates a shared gap at the insertion locus, shifting all rendered alignments after the break consistently instead of overlaying inserted bases on one row or shifting each read independently.
acceptance_criteria: Manual insertion expansion creates a shared visual gap at an insertion locus. All read rows use the same shifted coordinate mapping after the selected locus. Inserted bases render in the gap only for reads with sequence at that insertion. Collapsed mode remains a prominent insertion marker. Tests cover shared shifting and non-carrier gap behavior.
close_reason: Implemented shared-gap insertion expansion so all tracks/read rows shift consistently at the selected insertion locus.

title: Refine insertion visibility without alignment shifting
description: Expanded insertion rendering currently shifts downstream aligned bases, which makes alignments look out of register. Collapsed insertion markers are also too subtle. Refine insertion rendering so expansion does not shift downstream alignment columns and collapsed mode emphasizes insertion boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: Expanded insertion rendering does not shift downstream aligned bases. Collapsed insertion markers are more visually prominent than the current caret-only marker. Boundary bases around insertions remain emphasized. Renderer tests cover collapsed and expanded insertion behavior.
close_reason: Refined insertion rendering to avoid downstream alignment shifts and use a stronger collapsed insertion marker.

title: Add manual insertion expansion toggle
description: Expanded insertion rendering currently activates automatically at high zoom. Make insertions collapsed by default and add a manual toggle so users can expand inserted sequence in the current view only when requested.
acceptance_criteria: Insertions are collapsed by default. A keyboard command toggles expanded insertion rendering. Help and status text document the toggle. Existing insertion overwrite regression remains covered by tests.
close_reason: Added manual i-key insertion expansion toggle, collapsed default rendering, UI indicators, and tests.

title: Expand insertion rendering in current view
description: Insertions are currently collapsed to a caret and can be overwritten by adjacent aligned bases. Add current-view insertion expansion so inserted bases are visible and insertion boundary bases are emphasized with bold underline styling.
acceptance_criteria: Insertion sequence is rendered between the aligned boundary bases when base-level view has enough columns. Boundary bases flanking an insertion are bold and underlined. Insertion rendering does not get overwritten by following CIGAR operations. Existing non-insertion rendering behavior remains covered by tests.
close_reason: Implemented expanded base-level insertion rendering with bold underlined boundaries and regression tests.

title: Rename crate package to locus-tui
description: The crates.io package name locus is unavailable. Rename the publishable package to locus-tui while keeping the installed binary command as locus.
close_reason: Renamed publishable package to locus-tui while keeping the installed binary command as locus.

title: Use tabix-indexed annotation queries
description: When a sorted BGZF-compressed GFF/GTF has a tabix index, query visible regions through the index instead of scanning every loaded feature.
notes: Implemented indexed visible-region queries when a .tbi sidecar exists for a gzip/BGZF GFF/GTF. The store still builds the existing in-memory feature/name index for feature search; rendering no longer scans that vector when tabix query succeeds.
close_reason: Feature rendering now queries .tbi-indexed BGZF annotations for visible regions, with fallback to the prior linear scan and an indexed fixture test.

title: Add terminal screenshot capture
description: Add an in-app keybinding to save the current ratatui screen as a timestamped text screenshot file for sharing/debugging.
close_reason: Added s keybinding to save current ratatui screen to screenshots/locus-<timestamp>.txt and documented it

title: Clarify TUI top status bar
description: Make the top bar easier to scan by using consistent labeled fields and avoiding crowded status text.
close_reason: Top status bar now uses consistent labels, explicit scale/read metrics, and truncation for narrow terminals

title: Render model and pileup layout
description: cache.rs + render/: RenderRead, row-packing, coverage binning
close_reason: Closed

title: BAM source: open file, index, header
description: bam.rs: BamSource struct, open BAM+index, parse header, fetch reads
close_reason: Closed

title: Align selection brackets with base rendering
description: Make the toggleable fluorescent-green selection brackets available whenever individual bases are rendered, matching the insertion-expansion eligibility rule.
design: Reuse the shared base-render threshold rather than maintaining a separate selection-bracket zoom cutoff. Preserve the b toggle and double brackets for selected expanded insertions.
acceptance_criteria: At the 5 bp-per-column base-render boundary, an enabled selected base has green brackets; above that boundary it does not. The behavior is covered by a focused test and full Rust checks pass.
close_reason: Selection brackets now share the 5 bp-per-column base-render threshold with insertion expansion, reference, and read rendering; a UI boundary test verifies the enabled and disabled cases.

title: Expand insertions whenever bases are visible
description: Allow manual insertion expansion at every zoom level that renders individual read bases, rather than limiting it to one base per column.
design: Use the existing read base-render threshold as the single eligibility criterion. Keep insertion expansion manual through i and Tab and preserve the shared-gap transform.
acceptance_criteria: Visible insertion gaps and selected insertion expansion work at 5 bp/column; they remain unavailable above the base-render threshold; existing manual controls and shared alignment behavior remain unchanged.
close_reason: Insertion expansion now uses the read base-render threshold, so every base-visible zoom supports manual expansion; boundary tests cover both sides of the limit.

title: Add toggleable fluorescent selection brackets
description: Render selected base columns with non-destructive fluorescent-green brackets and show selected expanded insertions with a double bracket pair.
design: Reserve selection bracket columns in the shared ViewTransform so aligned bases remain intact. When the selected coordinate is an expanded insertion anchor, reserve a second insertion bracket pair instead of a separate base bracket. Bind b to toggle the marker.
acceptance_criteria: b toggles selection brackets; selected read bases show green brackets without overwriting sequence; clicking an expanded insertion displays [[sequence]] with fluorescent outer brackets; transforms, mouse mapping, docs, and tests stay correct.
close_reason: Added default-on toggleable fluorescent selection brackets and double-bracket rendering for selected expanded insertions, with transform, renderer, UI, and capture coverage.

title: Anchor insertion selection and show deleted alleles
description: Make the selected-position information bar represent deletions by their reference sequence and resolve expanded insertion clicks to the preceding reference base.
design: Keep insertion gap geometry at its post-insertion boundary; use an explicit preceding-base anchor for selection, cycling, styling, and tallies. Use FASTA reference bases for deleted alleles, retaining a generic deletion count when no reference is loaded.
acceptance_criteria: Deletion tallies display -ACT-style alleles when reference sequence is available; expanded insertion clicks select the preceding base, tally the insertion there, and visually highlight both anchor and inserted bases; focused tests cover the behavior.
close_reason: Deletion alleles now use the reference sequence, and expanded insertion selections resolve, tally, and highlight at the preceding base.

title: Resolve startup feature names with -r
description: Allow a bare --region/-r value such as RB1 to resolve through a supplied GFF/GTF at application startup, while retaining genomic-region and contig behavior.
design: Load annotations before resolving the initial region. Explicit coordinate strings and known BAM contigs take precedence. Otherwise use a case-insensitive annotation resolver that ranks exact identifiers/names first and gene records before child features, then use the same 10 percent padded interval as in-app feature navigation.
acceptance_criteria: locus bam -a annotation.gtf -r RB1 opens the padded RB1 interval; coordinate and bare-contig inputs retain existing behavior; missing feature names report a clear error; unit tests cover feature, contig, coordinate, ranking, and padding behavior.
close_reason: Implemented startup feature-name resolution for -r with annotation ranking, shared padding, documentation, unit coverage, and a terminal smoke test.

title: Improve top bar contrast and selection emphasis
description: Make the top bar easier to scan in dark and light themes, with a visually distinct selected-position and allele-tally section.
design: Use dedicated top-bar and selection-pane theme colors rather than changing global chrome. Treat selected coordinate and tally as a separately fitted span with priority over low-value mode labels while retaining MAPQ visibility.
acceptance_criteria: Both themes use higher-contrast top-bar colors; a selected coordinate and allele tally are bold and visually separated; narrow terminal fitting preserves the selected pane and MAPQ label; unit and dark/light capture checks pass.
close_reason: Added high-contrast dark/light top bars, a bold selected-allele pane, priority fitting, tests, and refreshed captures.

title: Tally alleles at selected read base
description: When a user clicks a reference position, show the per-position allele tally in the information bar. Count aligned bases (including substitutions), deletion coverage, and inserted sequence alleles using CIGAR-aware traversal of reads passing the active mapping-quality filter.
design: Reuse the shared reference-coordinate model. A selected insertion anchor records both the aligned base coverage and any inserted sequence at that boundary; CIGAR skips are excluded because they are splicing, not indels. Compute from all loaded reads that pass the active MAPQ filter so the tally is not distorted by display row capacity.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking a base reports canonical base counts plus DEL and inserted sequence alleles; substitutions are reflected in base counts; changing the MAPQ filter refreshes the tally; focused unit tests cover match/mismatch, insertion, deletion, skips, and MAPQ filtering.
close_reason: Implemented CIGAR-aware click selection tally with MAPQ filtering, tests, documentation, and refreshed demo captures.

title: Use spare phased-view height before hiding reads
description: Compact phase sections now leave unused read-area height after the final visible section, but the cache still hides reads using fixed HP1/HP2/Unphased row budgets. A section with fewer rows than its allocated budget does not donate that capacity to a section with hidden reads.
design: Keep HP1 and HP2 independently packed and retain the optional unphased section. Determine each group's packed rows, then distribute available row capacity so no read is hidden while any read-area row remains unused. Preserve group headers, deterministic order, MAPQ filtering, coordinate transforms, and per-section hidden counts.
acceptance_criteria: When a phased group has hidden reads and another group uses fewer than its provisional row allowance, available view rows are reassigned so the hidden reads render; no read remains hidden if the phased read area can fit it; genuinely depth-constrained views still report accurate per-section hidden counts; compact section geometry remains contiguous; focused cache/UI tests and the demo capture validate dark and light behavior.
notes: Replaced fixed per-section packing limits with a two-stage phased layout: pack each group up to the total available row budget, retain the established HP1/HP2/Unphased priority as an initial allocation, then reclaim every unused provisional row before truncating. Centralized the UI read-area geometry so App capacity exactly matches optional reference/GFF/coverage tracks. Added cache and geometry regressions plus a seven-read demo that fills three HP1 rows, HP2, and Unphased without a hidden-read notice. Regenerated and inspected dark/light captures. Validated cargo test --locked (102), strict Clippy, format/diff checks, capture script syntax, and samtools quickcheck.
close_reason: Reclaimed spare phased rows and synchronized cache capacity with the rendered read area.

title: Investigate missing pull_request synchronize runs
description: PR #15 received its initial Rust workflow on pull-request open, but pushing commit ab1aa59 to the same open PR did not create a new Actions run even though .github/workflows/rust.yml uses an unrestricted pull_request trigger. A manual workflow_dispatch for the exact branch succeeded, so the current PR head is green but automatic PR synchronization needs investigation.
design: First inspect repository Actions settings, event payload/history, workflow permissions, and whether the push source suppresses workflow dispatch. Reproduce with a disposable branch or future PR before changing the trigger. Avoid broadening secrets or permissions merely to force execution.
acceptance_criteria: A normal commit pushed to an open same-repository PR deterministically creates the Rust workflow run; the root cause and verification evidence are documented; if configuration changes are needed, both the full Rust and MSRV jobs run automatically on synchronize without duplicate or unsafe workflows.

title: Identify phase-set boundaries in phased tracks
description: Phased read tracks currently separate HP1 and HP2, but reads from different phase sets (PS tags) are visually indistinguishable within a haplotype track. Show clear phase-set boundaries so users can see where separate phasing blocks begin without losing existing insertion, methylation, MAPQ, or selection cues.
design: Retain the parsed PS tag on the render read and derive boundaries from changes in phase-set identity among packed rows within each phased section. Render a lightweight non-destructive boundary cue that spans the read region, is visible in dark and light themes, and does not consume a read row or alter coordinate transforms. Keep reads without a valid PS tag visibly neutral and avoid marking boundaries in the unphased section.
acceptance_criteria: When p is enabled, distinct PS values represented in HP1 or HP2 are visually separated or labeled at deterministic boundaries; the cue is absent in unphased mode/section and does not shift rows or bases; reads with missing or malformed PS remain supported; the phase-set cue coexists with insertion expansion, methylation, MAPQ styling, selection, and both themes; unit/rendered-frame coverage and dark/light demo captures validate the behavior.
notes: Rendered phase-set-aware HP1/HP2 headers and boundary overlays from parsed integer PS tags. Visible phase sets are deduplicated by ID, sorted by earliest visible read start, summarized in the track header, and labeled at their observed coordinate; rails use empty cells and underline occupied bases without changing rows or transforms. Unphased reads never receive PS cues. Added a second HP1 PS fixture plus parsing, layout, overlay, frame, dark/light capture, and documentation coverage. Validated cargo test --locked (99), strict Clippy, format check, diff check, capture-script syntax, and samtools quickcheck.
close_reason: Added visible PS block labels and non-destructive boundary rails to phased tracks.

title: Compact separated phased read tracks
description: When phased read tracks are enabled, the UI divides the entire read canvas into fixed HP1, HP2, and Unphased bands even when each group has only one packed row. This leaves large blank gaps between the section header and its bases.
design: Use the existing PhasePileupLayout row ranges to allocate each section one header row plus its actual packed-row count. The sections remain contiguous from the top of the read canvas and unused terminal height remains below the final section. Preserve headers for groups with hidden reads but no retained rows.
acceptance_criteria: With one visible row in HP1, HP2, and Unphased groups, each header is immediately followed by its read row; groups are contiguous and bounded; a dense layout still allocates every packed row; empty groups with hidden reads retain a one-line header; phase, insertion, methylation, click-selection, and both themes remain correct.
notes: Packed HP1, HP2, and optional unphased sections to their headers plus actual row counts; unused viewport height now remains below the final section. Added layout and rendered-frame regression coverage, regenerated dark and light demo captures, and verified with cargo test --locked (97), cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings, cargo fmt --all -- --check, git diff --check, bash -n capture scripts, and samtools quickcheck.
close_reason: Compacted phased sections to packed row counts and verified dark/light captures.

title: Modernize Rust dependencies
description: Update Locus's dependency graph to current supported releases without changing genome-browser behavior. Replace the three overlapping Noodles generations with one compatible family, remove unused dependencies, refresh the TUI and error libraries, codify the supported Rust version, and make CI run the complete quality gate.
design: First update and validate the direct dependency constraints with the compiler. Keep BAM/SAM, BGZF, Core, CSI, and Tabix on one mutually compatible Noodles release family and remove aliases after source migration. Upgrade Ratatui and Crossterm together. Separate a lockfile refresh from behavioral migration, add CI Clippy and an explicit MSRV job, then inspect demo captures and package the crate.
acceptance_criteria: Cargo tree contains one Noodles version per crate and no unused noodles-gff dependency; all source APIs compile against current bounds; rust-version and matching CI job are explicit; CI runs format, check, Clippy, and tests; BAM query, sparse-BAM startup, methylation, phasing, and indexed GFF behavior have regression coverage; demo dark/light captures remain legible; cargo package and cargo publish --dry-run pass.
notes: Updated to a unified Noodles graph (BAM 0.92, SAM 0.87, Core 0.20, BGZF 0.49, CSI 0.58, Tabix 0.64), removed unused noodles-gff and compatibility aliases, upgraded Ratatui 0.30.2 with only the Crossterm backend, upgraded Crossterm 0.29 and thiserror 2, declared Rust 1.97.1, added locked Clippy/MSRV Actions checks, and enabled weekly grouped Dependabot updates. Validated 95 tests, strict Clippy, fixtures, dark/light captures, cargo package, and cargo publish dry run.
close_reason: Modernized dependencies, unified the Noodles graph, tightened CI and Dependabot maintenance, and validated package/release artifacts.

title: Select genomic position with mouse click
description: Add left-click selection to the TUI genomic canvas. Convert the clicked terminal column through the active shared ViewTransform to a reference coordinate, including explicit behavior for expanded insertion gaps. Highlight the selected coordinate across visible read rows without obscuring base, indel, methylation, phase, or MAPQ cues, and show the selected contig and 1-based position in the top information bar.
design: Store an optional 0-based selected reference position in App. Reuse centralized UI geometry and ViewTransform column conversion so mouse hit testing matches rendering. Render a non-destructive per-cell selection modifier after each ReadsTrack, clipped to read rows and skipped for empty cells. Clear selection on navigation or contig changes.
acceptance_criteria: Left-clicking the genomic canvas selects a visible coordinate without refetching; clicks in selected insertion-gap cells map to the insertion anchor; occupied bases at that coordinate are visibly highlighted across all read tracks; the top bar shows the contig and 1-based position; overlays and UI chrome ignore clicks; selection clears when the view/contig changes; focused tests, full Rust checks, and dark/light captures pass.
notes: Implemented left-click genomic selection through a shared inverse ViewTransform, including expanded-gap anchor mapping. Added a non-destructive reverse/underline overlay for occupied read cells, top-bar pos:contig:1-based state, navigation clearing, help/README updates, and a capture-script mouse event. Validated 95 Rust tests, strict Clippy, fixture integrity, and inspected dark/light screenshots.
close_reason: Implemented mouse-driven genomic position selection with read-cell highlighting, top-bar coordinates, expanded insertion-anchor mapping, tests, documentation, and inspected dark/light captures.

title: Separate phased reads into haplotype tracks
description: When phased-read display is enabled, render HP1 and HP2 alignments in separate labeled pileup tracks instead of only changing read colors. Preserve coordinate packing within each track, retain a distinct unphased section so reads are not silently hidden or duplicated, keep MAPQ filtering and coverage semantics unchanged, and preserve insertion, methylation, mismatch, and theme behavior.
design: Partition MAPQ-passing visible read indices into HP1, HP2, and neutral groups. Greedily pack each group independently, concatenate the resulting rows for existing navigation/counting behavior, and retain explicit row ranges plus per-group hidden counts. The renderer divides the reads area into contiguous labeled bands using the same ViewTransform; HP1 and HP2 share the phased height, while an optional neutral band receives one fifth of available height with a two-line minimum. Coverage remains computed from all MAPQ-passing reads.
acceptance_criteria: The p toggle remains off by default; enabling it creates visibly separate HP1 and HP2 tracks with stable coordinate packing and clear labels; unphased reads remain visible in a neutral separated section; available row height is shared predictably without overlap; hidden-read accounting remains accurate; insertions, methylation, MAPQ filtering, coverage, screenshots, and both themes continue to work; focused and full tests pass.
notes: Implemented grouped cache layout, p-triggered relayout, labeled HP1/HP2/Unphased bands, row/hidden-count and geometry tests, README updates, and regenerated dark/light demo captures. The malformed demo alignment was moved to avoid overlapping the other neutral example in the single-row neutral band.
close_reason: Implemented and validated separate HP1/HP2 read tracks with a neutral fallback section, independent packing, accurate hidden counts, MAPQ-preserving relayout, and refreshed dark/light demo captures.

title: Add configurable MAPQ read filter
description: Add a minimum mapping-quality filter for visible BAM alignments. Expose --min-mapq <0-255> on the CLI with a default of 0, and add a TUI control that lets users set or clear the threshold without reopening the BAM. Apply the same threshold to pileup rows and coverage while retaining unfiltered fetched reads in the region cache so interactive changes only relayout the current view. Show the active threshold in the interface and document the command and key binding.
acceptance_criteria: CLI accepts --min-mapq 0 through 255 and rejects invalid values; the TUI can set the threshold and use 0 to disable it; reads below the threshold are excluded from pileup and coverage; changing the threshold does not refetch the BAM; active state is visible; focused and full tests pass.
close_reason: Added --min-mapq and a Q-key TUI prompt; filtering consistently updates visible read rows and coverage from cached reads, exposes active state, validates 0-255 input, preserves narrow top-bar identity, and is covered by CLI/cache/app/UI tests plus PTY smoke validation.

title: Add phased-read viewing
description: Add an initial phased-read display mode for haplotagged BAMs. Parse standard HP (haplotype) and PS (phase set) alignment tags, expose the values in the render model, and add a manual toggle that colors HP1, HP2, and unphased reads distinctly while preserving mismatch, indel, methylation, selection, and light/dark theme readability. Show a concise legend/status, decide whether haplotype grouping improves pileup scanability, and extend the small demo fixture plus tests to showcase the behavior.
acceptance_criteria: HP and PS tags are parsed safely; phase display is collapsed/off by default and manually toggleable; HP1, HP2, and unphased reads are distinguishable in both themes; existing overlays remain legible; tests cover tagged, untagged, and malformed records; README/demo screenshots document the feature.
notes: Implemented on codex/phased-read-view. Coordinate row packing remains stable when toggled. Integer HP/PS tags are parsed safely into ReadPhase; invalid, negative, and non-integer values fall back without error. p toggles phase display off/on without refetching. HP1, HP2, and unphased reads have distinct dark/light arrow and base-level palettes; MAPQ remains bold/normal/dim and mismatch, indel, and methylation styles retain precedence. Demo now includes HP1, HP2, untagged, and malformed reads, with regenerated compact dark/light captures. Validated cargo fmt --check, cargo check --locked, strict all-target clippy, 79 tests, bash syntax, samtools quickcheck, tag inspection, and rendered PNG inspection.
close_reason: Implemented and validated phased-read viewing with HP/PS parsing, p toggle, theme-aware rendering, tests, and demo captures.

title: Open unpositioned BAMs at first mapped read
description: When --region is omitted, startup currently opens bases 1-1000 of the first header contig, so sparse coordinate-sorted BAMs can appear empty. Read only the first mapped alignment after the BAM header and derive the default 1000 bp viewport from its contig and start. Explicit --region remains authoritative, and BAMs with no mapped alignments retain the existing first-contig fallback.
acceptance_criteria: Without --region, a sparse indexed BAM opens on its first mapped alignment; explicit --region behavior is unchanged; empty/all-unmapped BAMs do not fail startup; focused tests and existing quality gates pass.
close_reason: Startup now centers the default viewport on the first mapped BAM alignment when --region is omitted; explicit regions and no-alignment fallback remain unchanged, with fixture and boundary tests.

title: Bump patch version and dry-run cargo publish
close_reason: Bumped locus-tui to 0.2.1, narrowed package include to tracked docs/captures and docs/images to avoid ignored docs/screenshots artifacts, and verified cargo publish --dry-run successfully packaged and verified 46 files.

title: Clean up cargo clippy warnings
close_reason: Resolved cargo clippy warnings across app/cache/gff/render/main. Verified cargo fmt --all, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features with zero warnings, cargo test, and cargo check.

title: Bump crate version for recent UI features
close_reason: Bumped locus-tui package and lockfile versions to 0.2.0 after recent user-visible UI features. Verified cargo fmt --all, cargo check, and cargo test.

title: Add light mode rendering style
description: Add a light-background style option so terminal rendering and screenshots can show reads, methylation, insertions, features, and UI bars legibly on light backgrounds.
acceptance_criteria: Users can switch between default dark styling and light mode. Methylation, insertion, deletion, feature, and reference/read colors remain distinguishable. README/demo documentation mentions the light mode option. cargo fmt/check/test pass.
close_reason: Implemented light theme with --light startup flag, t runtime toggle, themed render tracks/screenshots/docs/demo captures. Verified cargo fmt --all, cargo check, cargo test, and cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features (warnings only).

title: Add demo dataset and README screenshots
description: Create a small committed example dataset plus rendered screenshots so README sections can showcase insertion expansion, methylation display, annotations, and screenshot/export behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Repository includes a small demo dataset or reproducible demo generator. README references feature-specific screenshots/artifacts and commands. Local cargo fmt/check/test pass before PR.
close_reason: Added a small demo dataset, reproducible build/capture scripts, app-generated screenshot artifacts, README image, and feature-specific README notes.

title: Add GitHub Actions Rust test workflow
description: Add repository CI so pull requests and branch pushes validate formatting/build/tests for the Rust TUI before merge.
acceptance_criteria: A GitHub Actions workflow runs cargo fmt --check, cargo check, and cargo test on pull requests and pushes. The workflow can also be run manually. Local cargo test passes before commit.
close_reason: Added Rust GitHub Actions workflow for fmt, check, and tests; local CI-equivalent gates pass.

title: Add methylation toggle UI
description: Add normal-mode UI state and keybinding for toggling methylation display on reads. The toggle should be discoverable in the bottom bar/help overlay and should not conflict with existing insertion expansion or feature-search controls.
design: Use a mnemonic key that does not conflict with current normal-mode controls. Candidate: m for methylation. Keep insertion expansion on i/Tab.
acceptance_criteria: Normal mode has a documented methylation toggle key. Top or bottom UI reflects whether methylation display is enabled. Toggle state does not refetch reads unnecessarily. Existing modes keep their current key behavior. UI/event tests or focused app-state tests cover the toggle.
close_reason: Implemented normal-mode methylation toggle UI on m with top/bottom/help discoverability and tests.

title: Validate methylation toggle with fixtures
description: Add test fixtures and coverage for methylation parsing, CIGAR mapping, rendering, and user-facing toggle behavior. Include at least one realistic MM/ML example and edge cases without modified-base tags.
design: Prefer small synthetic records or parser-level fixtures for MM/ML decoding, and renderer-level synthetic RenderRead values for visual tests. Avoid requiring large BAM fixtures unless a tiny indexed test BAM is already practical.
acceptance_criteria: Tests include reads with MM+ML, MM without ML, no methylation tags, reverse-strand reads, and CIGARs with insertion/deletion/soft clip. cargo test passes. README/help text documents the methylation toggle and any supported tag limitations.
close_reason: Added parser fixtures for empty and reverse-strand MM tags, renderer methylation fixtures, and README/help documentation; cargo test passes.

title: Parse MM/ML modified-base tags
description: Add BAM auxiliary tag parsing for SAM MM and ML tags so read methylation calls are available before rendering. Focus first on cytosine methylation calls commonly emitted by ONT/PacBio pipelines, while leaving the parser extensible for other modified bases.
design: Keep parsing isolated from terminal rendering, likely in bam.rs or a small methylation/modbase module. Convert probabilities to a compact u8 probability or normalized score. Do not assume every read has ML.
acceptance_criteria: MM tags are parsed for canonical base, strand, modification code, skip mode, and delta positions. ML probabilities are associated with parsed calls when present. Unsupported or malformed tags fail gracefully without dropping the read. Unit tests cover representative MM/ML examples and missing ML tags.
close_reason: Implemented MM/ML modified-base parsing, wired parsed calls into RenderRead, and added parser tests for probabilities, missing ML, skip modes, malformed tags, and out-of-range deltas.

title: Render methylation marks on reads
description: Add read-track rendering for methylation calls when methylation display is enabled. The visual style should be legible in terminal and HTML screenshots while preserving existing base colors and mismatch styling as much as practical.
design: Prefer background or modifier cues that do not erase the base letter. Avoid a one-note color palette; choose a methylation color that remains distinguishable from mismatch, insertion, deletion, and MAPQ dimming styles.
acceptance_criteria: Methylated and unmethylated calls have distinct visual treatments. Probability/confidence can be represented by intensity or a small set of bins. Rendering composes with reference mismatch styling and indel expansion. Screenshot HTML/ANSI output preserves the selected styles. Renderer tests cover styled methylated and unmethylated bases.
close_reason: Rendered methylation calls on read bases when enabled, with probability-dependent styling and insertion-expansion tests.

title: Map methylation calls through CIGAR
description: Map parsed modified-base calls from read coordinates onto aligned reference positions so the pileup renderer can show methylation on the correct visible base. The mapping must respect matches, mismatches, insertions, deletions, skips, and soft clips.
design: Reuse the existing CIGAR walk that already tracks read_pos/ref_pos in render logic, but perform methylation coordinate mapping before rendering so the renderer can look up calls by reference/read position cheaply.
acceptance_criteria: Modified-base calls on aligned read bases receive reference positions. Calls on inserted or soft-clipped bases are either retained with read-coordinate metadata or intentionally skipped with tests documenting the behavior. Mapping handles reverse-strand reads consistently with decoded sequence orientation. Unit tests cover CIGARs with insertions, deletions, skips, and soft clips.
close_reason: Added RenderRead methylation-to-reference mapping through CIGAR with tests for matches, soft clips, insertions, deletions, and skips.

title: Add read methylation display toggle
description: Plan and implement a read-level methylation display mode. The feature should parse modified-base BAM tags, preserve per-read methylation calls in the render model, and let users toggle methylation visualization on reads without disrupting existing base, mismatch, insertion, deletion, and feature rendering.
design: Use SAM/BAM MM/ML modified-base tags as the source of methylation calls. Store decoded calls on RenderRead in read-coordinate form plus enough metadata to render on reference-aligned bases. Rendering should be opt-in and should compose with existing mismatch and indel display rather than replacing core read layout.
acceptance_criteria: Users can toggle methylation display from normal mode. Reads with supported methylation tags show methylation state/probability in the pileup. Reads without methylation tags render unchanged. The feature is covered by parser, coordinate mapping, renderer, and UI tests.
close_reason: Implemented MM/ML parsing, CIGAR mapping, m-key UI toggle, read rendering, docs, and test coverage.

title: Cycle expanded insertion locus with Tab
description: Insertion expansion currently selects one visible insertion automatically. Add a normal-mode Tab shortcut to move the expanded shared-gap view to the next visible insertion locus, with Shift+Tab moving backward.
acceptance_criteria: Tab cycles to the next visible expanded insertion locus when insertion expansion is enabled. Shift+Tab cycles backward. The selected locus persists during rendering while visible. Status text reports the selected insertion position. Tests cover visible insertion gap ordering and selection behavior.
close_reason: Added normal-mode Tab/Shift+Tab cycling for the selected expanded insertion locus.

title: Box expanded insertion gaps
description: Expanded insertion gaps should be visually boxed so inserted sequence is distinguishable from deletions or empty gap cells. Add border columns around the shared insertion gap when expansion is active.
acceptance_criteria: Expanded insertion gaps reserve visible left and right border columns. Inserted bases render inside the bordered gap. Non-carrier reads show the same boxed gap region without inserted bases. Tests cover boxed expanded insertion rendering.
close_reason: Added bracketed border columns around expanded insertion gaps and removed gray inserted-base background.

title: Polish crate metadata for publishing
description: Cargo.toml has initial crates.io metadata that should be made accurate and committed without including local .codex files.
close_reason: Added publishing metadata, excluded local .codex files, and verified package contents.

title: Prepare annotation files for indexed browsing
description: Add an explicit workflow to sort, BGZF-compress, and tabix-index GFF3/GTF annotations when they are not already prepared.
close_reason: Added prepare-annotations subcommand that sorts GFF/GTF records, writes BGZF output, creates a .tbi index, and validates the prepared file through indexed region queries.

title: Polish screenshot export filenames and docs
description: Avoid timestamp collisions when saving screenshots and update documentation to reflect both ANSI text and HTML screenshot outputs.
close_reason: Screenshot filenames now include millisecond precision plus process id, and README describes both text and HTML outputs

title: Export HTML screenshots
description: Screenshots should include an HTML artifact that preserves ratatui cell colors in browsers and editors, while keeping the existing text screenshot export.
close_reason: Added HTML screenshot export alongside ANSI text screenshots with tests for styling and escaping.

title: Preserve colors in text screenshots
description: Text screenshots currently write only buffer symbols and discard ratatui cell styles. Emit ANSI SGR escape codes by default so catting a screenshot in an ANSI-aware terminal preserves colors.
close_reason: Text screenshot export now emits ANSI SGR styling by default and tests cover colored output.

title: Plan crates.io release publishing workflow
description: Plan only for later implementation: add a crates.io publishing workflow after first manual publish. Prefer Trusted Publishing via GitHub Actions OIDC on v* tags or GitHub Releases, with release environment protection and cargo publish --locked. Avoid publishing on every PR merge; keep main CI as format/check/test. Include fallback token-secret option only if Trusted Publishing is unavailable. Prereqs: first manual cargo publish, crates.io trusted publisher configured for bwbioinfo/locus workflow/environment, and documented version/tag release process.
